name: CISSP dump (reviewed) - Domain 4: Communication and Network Security

questions.stem: At what level of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model is data at rest on a Storage Area Network (SAN) located?
questions.explanation: Data at rest on SAN media resides physically on storage devices, the physical layer.
optionNotes: Link layer covers framing in transit.
Correct: stored data resides on physical media.
Session layer manages dialogs.
Application layer is user services.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors contributes to the weakness of Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol?
options: WEP uses a small range Initialization Vector (IV)
WEP does not use any Initialization Vector (IV)
questions.explanation: WEP's 24-bit IV is too small, causing reuse and key recovery.
optionNotes: Correct: 24-bit IV repeats, enabling key recovery.
WEP uses CRC-32, not MD5.
WEP has no Diffie-Hellman exchange.
WEP does use an IV.

questions.stem: Which of the following operates at the Network Layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model?
questions.explanation: Packet filtering examines IP addresses, a network-layer function.
optionNotes: Correct: filters by IP addresses at layer 3.
Ports are transport layer.
Content inspection is application layer.
Application-layer control.

questions.stem: An external attacker has compromised an organization's network security perimeter and installed a sniffer onto an inside computer. Which of the following is the MOST effective layer of security the organization could have implemented to mitigate the attacker's ability to gain further information?
options: Implement packet filtering on the network firewalls
Install Host Based Intrusion Detection Systems (HIDS)
Implement logical network segmentation at the switches
questions.explanation: Logical segmentation (VLANs) limits what traffic a sniffer on one segment can observe.
optionNotes: Perimeter firewall doesn't stop internal sniffing.
HIDS detects but doesn't limit capture.
Admin auth doesn't stop passive sniffing.
Correct: segmentation limits traffic visible to the sniffer.

questions.stem: In a Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) stack, which layer is responsible for negotiating and establishing a connection with another node?
questions.explanation: In the TCP/IP model the transport layer (TCP handshake) establishes connections.
optionNotes: Correct: TCP handshake at transport layer.
Application layer uses connections, doesn't establish them.
Network layer is routing, connectionless.
No session layer in TCP/IP model.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used by the Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) to determine packet formats?
questions.explanation: PPP's LCP negotiates link options including packet format.
optionNotes: L2TP is tunneling, not PPP format negotiation.
Correct: LCP negotiates link and packet options.
CHAP authenticates.
Not a real PPP component.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an Internet Protocol (IP) spoofing attack?
options: To send excessive amounts of data to a process, making it unpredictable
To intercept network traffic without authorization
To disguise the destination address from a target's IP filtering devices
To convince a system that it is communicating with a known entity
questions.explanation: IP spoofing forges a source address to appear as a trusted, known host.
optionNotes: Describes buffer overflow/flooding.
Describes sniffing.
Spoofing forges source, not destination.
Correct: impersonates a trusted host.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered best practice for preventing e-mail spoofing?
questions.explanation: Digitally signing email (e.g. S/MIME, DKIM) proves origin and prevents spoofing. Spam filters and reverse DNS lookups are heuristics that a spoofer can evade. A digital signature cryptographically binds the message to the sender, so forged mail fails verification.
optionNotes: Spam filtering reduces junk but cannot prove sender identity.
Right: digital signatures prove origin and integrity of mail.
URL filtering blocks links, not spoofed senders.
Reverse DNS is a weak heuristic, easily defeated.

questions.stem: Which Hyper Text Markup Language 5 (HTML5) option presents a security challenge for network data leakage prevention and/or monitoring?
questions.explanation: WebSockets open persistent bidirectional channels that bypass usual HTTP inspection, hindering DLP/monitoring. CORS (A) still runs over ordinary, inspectable HTTP requests. A WebSocket keeps a persistent two-way channel open that many DLP and proxy tools cannot parse, so data can leave unseen.
optionNotes: CORS controls cross-origin requests; still HTTP and visible.
Right: persistent WebSocket channels bypass normal HTTP inspection, hiding data flows.
DOM trees are a client-side structure, not a transport.
Web IDL is an interface spec language.

questions.stem: Which one of the following effectively obscures network addresses from external exposure when implemented on a firewall or router?
questions.explanation: NAT hides internal addresses behind public ones. An application proxy (B) hides clients only for proxied protocols. NAT rewrites internal addresses to public ones for all traffic, so internal addressing is never exposed.
optionNotes: Right: NAT hides internal addresses behind public ones.
Proxies hide clients at application layer but NAT is the network address answer.
RIP v2 is a routing protocol, exposes routes.
Address masking is not a standard hiding method.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the key exchange for Internet Protocol Security (IPSec)?
questions.explanation: IKE is the IPsec key exchange protocol. SSL (A) has its own handshake unrelated to IPsec. IKE negotiates IPsec security associations and keys.
optionNotes: SSL has its own handshake, not IPsec.
Right: IKE negotiates IPsec SAs and keys.
SKE is not the IPsec standard.
ICMP is for control messages.

questions.stem: An organization allows ping traffic into and out of their network. An attacker has installed a program on the network that uses the payload portion of the ping packet to move data into and out of the network. What type of attack has the organization experienced?
questions.explanation: Hiding data in ICMP payloads is a covert channel. Data leakage (A) describes the outcome, not the technique. Hiding data inside allowed ICMP payloads uses a channel not intended for communication, which is a covert channel.
optionNotes: Data leakage is a general outcome, not the attack technique.
Not a standard term.
Emanation is unintended signal leakage.
Right: abusing ICMP payloads hides communication in a covert channel.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a security limitation of File Transfer Protocol (FTP)?
options: Passive FTP is not compatible with web browsers.
FTP uses Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) ports 20 and 21.
questions.explanation: FTP transmits usernames and passwords in cleartext, so anyone sniffing the path can capture credentials. Secure alternatives such as SFTP or FTPS fix this.
optionNotes: Browser compatibility is a usability matter, not security
Anonymous access is an optional configuration, not inherent
Using ports 20/21 is simply how FTP works
Right: cleartext authentication exposes credentials

questions.stem: Which one of the following considerations has the LEAST impact when considering transmission security?
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is mainly a performance and capacity concern. Availability, data integrity and node locations (physical exposure, interception points) bear directly on transmission security.
optionNotes: Availability is a core security objective
Integrity of transmitted data is central
Right: performance concern, least security impact
Node locations affect physical exposure and interception

questions.stem: Which of the following is a security feature of Global Systems for Mobile Communications (GSM)?
options: It uses a Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) for authentication.
It uses encrypting techniques for all communications.
The radio spectrum is divided with multiple frequency carriers.
The signal is difficult to read as it provides end-to-end encryption.
questions.explanation: GSM authenticates subscribers with a secret key Ki stored in the SIM in a challenge-response with the network. Encryption covers only the radio link, not end to end.
optionNotes: Right: SIM-based authentication
Encryption covers only handset to base station
Frequency division is a radio technique, not security
GSM has no end-to-end encryption

questions.stem: The FIRST step in building a firewall is to
options: assign the roles and responsibilities of the firewall administrators.
define the intended audience who will read the firewall policy.
identify mechanisms to encourage compliance with the policy.
perform a risk analysis to identify issues to be addressed.
questions.explanation: A firewall design should follow from a risk analysis of what needs protecting and from which threats. Policy, roles and compliance steps come after that.
optionNotes: Assigning administrators comes later
Audience of the policy is a documentation detail
Compliance mechanisms follow policy creation
Right: risk analysis drives firewall requirements

questions.stem: A disadvantage of an application filtering firewall is that it can lead to
options: a crash of the network as a result of user activities.
performance degradation due to the rules applied.
loss of packets on the network due to insufficient bandwidth.
questions.explanation: Application-level firewalls inspect payloads in depth and often proxy connections. That processing cost causes performance degradation compared with packet filters.
optionNotes: User activity does not typically crash the network via the firewall
Right: deep inspection costs throughput
Bandwidth shortage is unrelated to filtering type
Proxies make spoofing harder, not easier

questions.stem: Internet Protocol (IP) source address spoofing is used to defeat
questions.explanation: Forging a trusted source IP address defeats systems that grant access based on source address, such as rhosts or IP whitelists.
optionNotes: Right: trust based on IP is bypassed
ARP maps IP to MAC; spoofing IP does not defeat it
RARP is an obsolete address-discovery protocol
Spoofing is a component of TCP hijacking, not a defence against it

questions.stem: By allowing storage communications to run on top of Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) with a Storage Area Network (SAN), the
options: confidentiality of the traffic is protected.
opportunity to sniff network traffic exists.
opportunity for device identity spoofing is eliminated.
storage devices are protected against availability attacks.
questions.explanation: Carrying storage protocols such as iSCSI over TCP/IP puts storage traffic on a shared IP network. Without added encryption that traffic can be sniffed.
optionNotes: IP transport adds no confidentiality by itself
Right: storage traffic becomes sniffable
IP exposes devices to spoofing rather than removing it
IP networks bring availability attacks too

questions.stem: Checking routing information on e-mail to determine it is in a valid format and contains valid information is an example of which of the following anti-spam approaches?
questions.explanation: Checking that received and routing headers are well-formed and consistent is header analysis.
optionNotes: Blacklists match sender IPs/domains against bad lists
Reverse DNS checks the sender IP's PTR record only
Hashing fingerprints message content
Right: inspects routing information in headers

questions.stem: In a basic SYN flood attack, what is the attacker attempting to achieve?
options: Exceed the threshold limit of the connection queue for a given service
Set the threshold to zero for a given service
Cause the buffer to overflow, allowing root access
Flush the register stack, allowing hijacking of the root account
questions.explanation: A SYN flood leaves many half-open connections that fill the server's backlog queue. Once the queue is full, legitimate connection requests are refused.
optionNotes: Right: exhausts the connection queue
Attackers cannot set service thresholds
Describes buffer overflow, not SYN flood
Not how SYN floods work

questions.stem: An advantage of link encryption in a communications network is that it
options: makes key management and distribution easier.
protects data from start to finish through the entire network.
improves the efficiency of the transmission.
encrypts all information, including headers and routing information.
questions.explanation: Link encryption encrypts the entire frame, including headers and routing data, on each hop. This also resists traffic analysis.
optionNotes: Many links make key management harder
That describes end-to-end encryption; link encryption decrypts at each node
Encryption adds overhead
Right: headers and routing info are encrypted

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE for point-to-point microwave transmissions?
options: They are not subject to interception due to encryption.
Interception only depends on signal strength.
They are too highly multiplexed for meaningful interception.
They are subject to interception by an antenna within proximity.
questions.explanation: Microwave links are radio transmissions; anyone placing an antenna in or near the beam path can intercept the signal.
optionNotes: Microwave links are not inherently encrypted
Antenna placement in the beam path matters, not only strength
Multiplexing is easily demultiplexed by an interceptor
A nearby antenna in the path can capture the signal

questions.stem: Which of the following does the Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) provide?
questions.explanation: ESP encrypts the payload (confidentiality) and can authenticate it (integrity); AH alone provides integrity without confidentiality.
optionNotes: ESP offers no authorization; access decisions are outside IPsec
Availability is not an ESP service; ESP can't stop DoS
ESP encrypts the payload and its ICV authenticates it
Authorization is not an ESP function, though ESP does encrypt

questions.stem: What is the term commonly used to refer to a technique of authenticating one machine to another by forging packets from a trusted source?
questions.explanation: Forging packets so they appear to come from a trusted source is spoofing.
optionNotes: MITM intercepts/relays between two parties rather than forging a trusted source
Smurf is ICMP broadcast amplification DoS
Session redirect diverts an existing session path
Forging source addresses to appear trusted is spoofing

questions.stem: Which one of the following transmission media is MOST effective in preventing data interception?
questions.explanation: Fiber carries light, emits no EMI and is very hard to tap without detection.
optionNotes: Microwave is broadcast radio, easily received
Twisted pair radiates and can be tapped by induction
Light in glass emits no EMI and taps cause measurable loss
Coax can be tapped with vampire taps

questions.stem: Which layer of the Open Systems Interconnections (OSI) model implementation adds information concerning the logical connection between the sender and receiver?
questions.explanation: The transport layer establishes and manages end-to-end logical connections (ports, sequence numbers) between sender and receiver. The OPT4 datagram item is a different question.
optionNotes: Physical layer handles bits on the medium
Session layer manages dialogues, not connection headers
Transport headers (ports, sequencing) manage the end-to-end logical connection
Data link frames are hop-by-hop on a local segment

questions.stem: Two companies wish to share electronic inventory and purchase orders in a supplier and client relationship. What is the BEST security solution for them?
options: Write a Service Level Agreement (SLA) for the two companies.
Set up a Virtual Private Network (VPN) between the two companies.
Configure a firewall at the perimeter of each of the two companies.
Establish a File Transfer Protocol (FTP) connection between the two companies.
questions.explanation: A site-to-site VPN protects the confidentiality and integrity of the exchanged business data.
optionNotes: An SLA is contractual and doesn't protect data in transit
A VPN encrypts and authenticates traffic between the companies
Perimeter firewalls don't protect data crossing the internet
FTP sends data and credentials in cleartext

questions.stem: Which of the following is a MAJOR consideration in implementing a Voice over IP (VoIP) network?
options: Use of separation for the voice network.
Use of Network Access Control (NAC) on switches.
Use of Request for Comments (RFC) 1918 addressing.
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] VoIP needs isolation of voice traffic for quality of service and to limit attacks such as eavesdropping and toll fraud from the data network. Separating the voice network (e.g., dedicated VLANs) is the major design consideration.
optionNotes: A feature choice, not a major security/design consideration.
Correct: separating voice from data protects QoS and limits attack exposure.
NAC is useful generally but is not the key VoIP consideration.
Private addressing is a routing detail, not a VoIP-specific concern.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides effective management assurance for a Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN)?
options: Maintaining an inventory of authorized Access Points (AP) and connecting devices
Setting the radio frequency to the minimum range required
Establishing a Virtual Private Network (VPN) tunnel between the WLAN client device and a VPN concentrator
Verifying that all default passwords have been changed
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] Management assurance comes from administrative oversight that confirms the environment is as intended. An inventory of authorized APs and devices lets management detect rogue APs and unauthorized clients; the others are technical configurations.
optionNotes: Correct: an inventory is a management control giving assurance over the WLAN.
A technical tuning measure, not management assurance.
A technical protection for traffic, not management assurance.
A configuration hardening step, not ongoing assurance.

questions.stem: A large university needs to enable student access to university resources from their homes. Which of the following provides the BEST option for low maintenance and ease of deployment?
options: Provide students with Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) Virtual Private Network (VPN) client software.
Use Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) VPN technology.
Use Secure Shell (SSH) with public/private keys.
Require students to purchase home router capable of VPN.
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS VPNs use a standard browser, need little or no client software and are easy to deploy to many users.
optionNotes: IPSec clients require installation and support.
Correct: clientless, browser-based and low maintenance.
Key management for thousands of students is burdensome.
Places burden and cost on students.

questions.stem: When implementing a secure wireless network, which of the following supports authentication and authorization for individual client endpoints.
options: Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP)
questions.explanation: WPA2 Enterprise uses 802.1X/EAP with a RADIUS server to authenticate and authorize each client individually.
optionNotes: TKIP is an encryption protocol.
PSK uses a shared key for all clients.
Correct: 802.1X gives per-client authentication.
CCMP is an encryption protocol.

questions.stem: From a security perspective, which of the following is a best practice to configure a Domain Name Service (DNS) system?
options: Configure secondary servers to use the primary server as a zone forwarder.
Block all Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connections.
Disable all recursive queries on the name servers.
Limit zone transfers to authorized devices.
questions.explanation: Zone transfers expose the full DNS map of a domain. Restricting them to authorized secondary servers is a standard DNS hardening practice.
optionNotes: A forwarding design, not a security practice.
DNS needs TCP for large responses and transfers.
Recursion may be needed on internal resolvers.
Correct: limiting zone transfers prevents reconnaissance.

questions.stem: A thorough review of an organization's audit logs finds that a disgruntled network administrator has intercepted emails meant for the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and changed them before forwarding them to their intended recipient. What type of attack has MOST likely occurred?
questions.explanation: Intercepting messages, altering them, and forwarding them on to the intended recipient is a man-in-the-middle attack.
optionNotes: Spoofing means faking identity, not intercepting and altering.
Eavesdropping is passive, but messages were changed.
Right: intercept, alter, forward is man-in-the-middle.
Messages were delivered, so there was no denial of service.

questions.stem: If an attacker in a SYN flood attack uses someone else's valid host address as the source address, the system under attack will send a large number of Synchronize/Acknowledge (SYN/ACK) packets to the
questions.explanation: The SYN/ACK replies go to the spoofed source address in the SYN packets, so the innocent host is flooded with backscatter.
optionNotes: The gateway isn't the target of the replies.
The attacker spoofed the address, so replies don't reach them.
The attacked interface sends the SYN/ACKs; it doesn't receive them.
Right: replies go to the spoofed source address.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST solution to provide redundancy for telecommunications links?
options: Provide multiple links from the same telecommunications vendor.
Ensure that the telecommunications links connect to the network in one location.
Ensure that the telecommunications links connect to the network in multiple locations.
Provide multiple links from multiple telecommunications vendors.
questions.explanation: Multiple vendors avoid a single carrier failure, giving the best telecom redundancy (route diversity).
optionNotes: One vendor is still a single point of failure.
A single entry point is a single point of failure.
Multiple entry points help, but one carrier can still fail.
Right: multiple carriers give the most diversity.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN feature that onion routing networks offer?
questions.explanation: Onion routing (such as Tor) layers encryption across relays to give users anonymity.
optionNotes: Onion routing hides identity, the opposite of non-repudiation.
Traceability is what it defeats.
Right: layered relays give anonymity.
Resilience is a side effect, not the main feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY concern when using an Internet browser to access a cloud-based service?
options: Insecure implementation of Application Programming Interfaces (API)
Improper use and storage of management keys
Misconfiguration of infrastructure allowing for unauthorized access
Vulnerabilities within protocols that can expose confidential data
questions.explanation: A browser reaches cloud services over web protocols such as HTTP/TLS, so protocol weaknesses that expose data in transit are the main concern for this access method. The other items are provider-side concerns not specific to browser use.
optionNotes: API security is relevant to programmatic access, not browser use
Key management is a provider/admin concern, not the browser channel
Infrastructure misconfiguration is a provider-side issue
Browser access depends on web protocols whose flaws can expose confidential data

questions.stem: Which of the following methods can be used to achieve confidentiality and integrity for data in transit?
questions.explanation: IPsec's ESP provides encryption for confidentiality and integrity checks, with AH adding integrity. It protects data in transit at the network layer.
optionNotes: MPLS separates traffic but does not encrypt or verify integrity
IPsec provides confidentiality and integrity in transit
Federated identity concerns authentication across domains
MFA strengthens authentication, not data protection in transit

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of Secure Socket Layer (SSL) and Transport Layer Security (TLS)?
options: SSL and TLS provide a generic channel security mechanism on top of Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).
SSL and TLS provide nonrepudiation by default.
SSL and TLS do not provide security for most routed protocols.
SSL and TLS provide header encapsulation over HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP).
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS sit above TCP and provide a generic secure channel that any application protocol can use. They do not provide nonrepudiation by default.
optionNotes: Correct: a generic secure channel over TCP
Nonrepudiation needs digital signatures on data, which TLS does not provide
Misleading claim; TLS secures application traffic over TCP, unrelated to routing
TLS does not encapsulate HTTP headers; it secures the whole stream

questions.stem: The PRIMARY characteristic of a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack is that it
options: exploits weak authentication to penetrate networks.
can be detected with signature analysis.
is commonly confused with viruses or worms.
questions.explanation: DDoS traffic is often made up of many legitimate-looking requests from distributed sources, which makes it hard to tell apart from real users. That is its defining difficulty.
optionNotes: DDoS targets availability, not authentication
Many DDoS floods have no unique signature
Traffic resembling normal activity is its key characteristic
Confusion with malware is not a characteristic

questions.stem: Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption protects
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS encrypts data in transit between endpoints. It does not protect stored data or hide the IP address.
optionNotes: SSL does not protect stored data
IP headers remain visible
SSL encrypts data in transmission
Encryption does not provide availability

questions.stem: Which of the following is a weakness of Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP)?
questions.explanation: WEP's 24-bit IV is too short, so IVs repeat quickly, which allows keystream reuse and key recovery. The other options describe protections WEP lacked, not weaknesses.
optionNotes: The short 24-bit IV is WEP's core flaw
Replay protection is something WEP lacks, so it isn't a weakness of it
Tamper detection is a feature WEP did poorly, not one it had
WEP had no key rotation; listing it as a feature is wrong

questions.stem: How does Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) in transport mode affect the Internet Protocol (IP)?
options: Encrypts and optionally authenticates the IP header, but not the IP payload
Encrypts and optionally authenticates the IP payload, but not the IP header
Authenticates the IP payload and selected portions of the IP header
Encrypts and optionally authenticates the complete IP packet
questions.explanation: In transport mode, ESP encrypts and optionally authenticates the IP payload but leaves the original IP header unprotected. Tunnel mode protects the whole original packet.
optionNotes: ESP never encrypts only the header
Transport mode protects the payload, not the header
This describes AH, which authenticates parts of the header
Whole-packet protection is tunnel mode

questions.stem: Application of which of the following Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) standards will prevent an unauthorized wireless device from being attached to a network?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.1X gives port-based network access control: devices must authenticate before they are allowed onto the network.
optionNotes: 802.1F concerns management information
802.1H concerns bridging/translation
802.1Q is VLAN tagging
802.1X authenticates devices before network access

questions.stem: A health care provider is considering Internet access for their employees and patients. Which of the following is the organization's MOST secure solution for protection of data?
options: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and digital signatures
questions.explanation: PKI with digital signatures provides strong authentication, integrity and non-repudiation for sensitive health data. It is stronger than any password-based option.
optionNotes: PKI and signatures provide the strongest assurance
Server certs plus passphrases are weaker
ID/password is weakest
Asymmetric encryption with only a user ID lacks strong user authentication

questions.stem: In general, servers that are facing the Internet should be placed in a demilitarized zone (DMZ). What is MAIN purpose of the DMZ?
options: Prepare the server for potential attacks.
Mitigate the risk associated with the exposed server.
Bypass the need for a firewall.
questions.explanation: A DMZ isolates exposed servers so their compromise poses less risk to internal systems.
optionNotes: DMZ isolates exposed servers to reduce risk to internal systems
DMZ does not prepare servers for attacks
The exposed server stays exposed; protection is for the internal network
A DMZ is built with firewalls, not instead of them

questions.stem: Data leakage of sensitive information is MOST often concealed by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Encrypted SSL/TLS channels hide exfiltrated data from inspection tools, concealing leakage.
optionNotes: SSL encryption hides exfiltrated data from inspection
SHA is hashing; it does not conceal data in transit
WEP is weak and limited to WLAN links
'Secure POP' is not a common concealment channel

questions.stem: The 802.1x standard provides a framework for what?
options: Network authentication for only wireless networks
Network authentication for wired and wireless networks
Wireless encryption using the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
Wireless network encryption using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.1X is port-based network access control for both wired and wireless networks.
optionNotes: 802.1X is not limited to wireless
Port-based authentication for wired and wireless
AES encryption is WPA2/802.11i, not 802.1X
802.1X does not use SSL for wireless encryption

questions.stem: What type of wireless network attack BEST describes an Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) attack?
questions.explanation: An EMP overwhelms or damages radio and electronic equipment, making the wireless network unavailable. Its effect is loss of availability, which is a denial of service.
optionNotes: RF describes the medium, not the attack's impact category.
Right: the result is loss of availability.
EMP does not selectively modify data.
EMP acts physically, not at the application layer.

questions.stem: In the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model, which layer is responsible for the transmission of binary data over a communications network?
questions.explanation: The Physical layer converts bits into electrical, optical or radio signals on the medium. Higher layers deal with frames, packets and application data.
optionNotes: Application layer serves user processes.
Right: transmits raw bits over the medium.
Data Link deals with frames and MAC addressing.
Network layer handles logical addressing and routing.

questions.stem: What is the BEST way to encrypt web application communications?
options: Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code (CBC-MAC)
questions.explanation: TLS is the current standard protocol for encrypting HTTP traffic. SSL is deprecated and insecure, while SHA-1 and CBC-MAC do not provide encryption.
optionNotes: SHA-1 is a hash, not encryption.
SSL is obsolete and vulnerable.
CBC-MAC provides integrity, not confidentiality.
Right: modern standard for web encryption.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a remote access protocol that uses a static authentication?
questions.explanation: PAP sends a fixed username and password, in clear text, once at connection setup. CHAP uses a changing challenge-response instead.
optionNotes: Tunneling protocol, not an authentication method.
Routing protocol.
Right: static, cleartext credentials.
Dynamic challenge-response, not static.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a recommended alternative to an integrated email encryption system?
options: Send sensitive data in separate emails
Encrypt sensitive data separately in attachments
Store sensitive information to be sent in encrypted drives
questions.explanation: If no integrated mail encryption is available, encrypting the sensitive file before attaching it still protects its contents in transit and at rest. The other options do not provide confidentiality in email.
optionNotes: Signing gives integrity, not confidentiality.
Splitting data does not protect it.
Right: encrypted attachments protect content.
Drives do not solve email transmission.

questions.stem: At which layer of the Open Systems Interconnect (OSI) model are the source and destination address for a datagram handled?
questions.explanation: The Network layer handles logical (IP) source and destination addressing for routing packets. Transport uses ports and Data Link uses MAC addresses.
optionNotes: Transport uses ports.
Data Link uses MAC frames.
Right: IP addressing.
Application does not address packets.

questions.stem: Which of the following adds end-to-end security inside a Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) connection?
questions.explanation: L2TP/IPSec protects the tunnel between gateways, but TLS between the application endpoints adds end-to-end protection inside it. SHA and TKIP are not end-to-end session protocols here.
optionNotes: TKIP is wireless only.
Hash, not session protection.
SSH secures specific shell sessions, less general.
Right: TLS gives application end-to-end security.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a rogue Access Point (AP)?
options: An AP that is not protected by a firewall
An AP not configured to use Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) with Triple Data Encryption Algorithm (3DES)
An AP connected to the wired infrastructure but not under the management of authorized network administrators
An AP infected by any kind of Trojan or Malware
questions.explanation: A rogue AP is one plugged into the wired network without authorization or management by the network team. It creates an unmanaged back door into the network.
optionNotes: Not being behind a firewall does not make an AP rogue.
WEP never used 3DES, and the encryption setting does not define rogue status.
Correct: an unauthorized, unmanaged AP connected to the wired network.
An infected AP is compromised, not necessarily rogue.

questions.stem: Which of the following secures web transactions at the Transport Layer?
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS works at the transport layer to secure web sessions such as HTTPS. S-HTTP secures individual messages at the application layer.
optionNotes: S-HTTP is application-layer, message-based security.
Correct: SSL secures web transactions at the transport layer.
SOCKS is a proxy protocol, not encryption.
SSH secures remote shells, not web transactions.

questions.stem: When using Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunneling over Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4), where is the GRE header inserted?
options: Between the delivery header and payload
Between the source and destination addresses
questions.explanation: GRE encapsulates the original packet. The GRE header sits between the outer delivery IP header and the encapsulated payload.
optionNotes: The options field is not used.
Correct: the GRE header sits between the delivery header and the payload.
It is not inserted inside the address fields.
The destination address is not modified to hold it.

questions.stem: Which of the following are effective countermeasures against passive network-layer attacks?
options: Federated security and authenticated access controls
Trusted software development and run time integrity controls
Enclave boundary protection and computing environment defense
questions.explanation: Passive attacks such as sniffing just observe traffic. Encryption, including security-enabled applications, makes the captured data unreadable.
optionNotes: Access controls do not stop passive eavesdropping.
Software integrity counters active tampering.
Correct: encryption defeats passive interception.
Boundary protection targets active intrusion.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY goal for using Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) to sign records?
questions.explanation: DNSSEC digitally signs DNS records so resolvers can verify they are authentic and unaltered, which prevents cache poisoning. It does not encrypt.
optionNotes: Correct: signatures provide integrity and origin authenticity.
DNSSEC does not encrypt queries.
Accountability is not its goal.
Availability is not improved by signing.

questions.stem: What type of encryption is used to protect sensitive data in transit over a network?
questions.explanation: Data in transit is protected by encrypting the payload (end to end) and/or the transport channel, for example with TLS or IPsec. AH provides integrity, not encryption.
optionNotes: Correct: payload and transport encryption protect data in transit.
AH gives integrity and authentication, not confidentiality.
HMAC provides integrity, not encryption.
P2PE is specific to payment-card terminals.

questions.stem: Which one of the following activities would present a significant security risk to organizations when employing a Virtual Private Network (VPN) solution?
options: Users with Internet Protocol (IP) addressing conflicts
questions.explanation: Split tunnelling, being connected to the VPN and another network at once, lets an attacker on the untrusted network bridge into the corporate network through the remote host. That is the classic VPN-specific risk; the other items are operational or general privilege issues.
optionNotes: Bandwidth is a performance concern, not a security exposure.
Correct: simultaneous connections (split tunnelling) bridge untrusted networks into the VPN.
IP conflicts cause connectivity problems, not a significant security risk.
Admin rights are a general endpoint risk, not specific to the VPN connection.

questions.stem: A proxy firewall operates at what layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model?
questions.explanation: Proxy (application-level gateway) firewalls terminate and inspect connections at the application layer, understanding protocol content.
optionNotes: Transport is where circuit-level gateways work.
Data link is used by MAC filtering devices.
Network is where packet filters operate.
Correct: proxies operate at layer 7.

questions.stem: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack on a syslog server exploits weakness in which of the following protocols?
options: Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) and Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)
Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) and Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP)
Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)
questions.explanation: Syslog runs over UDP 514 (and TCP in reliable variants); flooding these transport protocols overwhelms the server.
optionNotes: PPP/ICMP are not syslog transports.
Correct: syslog uses UDP/TCP, which floods exploit.
ARP/RARP are link-layer address protocols.
TLS/SSL secure transport and are not the default syslog weakness.

questions.stem: What protocol is often used between gateway hosts on the Internet?
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior routing protocol used between autonomous systems on the Internet.
optionNotes: EGP is obsolete.
Correct: BGP.
OSPF is interior.
ICMP is not routing.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the MOST comprehensive filtering of Peer-to-Peer (P2P) traffic?
questions.explanation: An application proxy inspects traffic at layer 7, so it can identify P2P protocols even when they hop ports or tunnel over common ports.
optionNotes: Correct: layer-7 inspection identifies P2P protocols whatever port they use
Port filters are defeated by P2P port hopping/tunnelling over 80/443
Boundary routers filter on addresses/ports, not application content
Access switches work at layer 2 and do not filter applications

questions.stem: What is the BEST location in a network to place Virtual Private Network (VPN) devices when an internal review reveals network design flaws in remote access?
options: In its own separate Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN)
questions.explanation: Terminating VPNs in a dedicated DMZ lets decrypted remote traffic be inspected and filtered before it reaches the internal network.
optionNotes: Correct: a dedicated DMZ lets decrypted VPN traffic be filtered before it reaches inside
A VLAN alone gives weak separation with no firewall inspection
Placing it at the ISP removes the organization's control of the endpoint
Outside the firewall leaves the device unprotected and its traffic uninspected

questions.stem: A post-implementation review has identified that the Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) system was designed to have gratuitous Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) disabled. Why did the network architect likely design the VoIP system with gratuitous ARP disabled?
options: Gratuitous ARP requires the use of Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) 1.
Gratuitous ARP requires the use of insecure layer 3 protocols.
Gratuitous ARP increases the likelihood of a successful brute-force attack on the phone.
Gratuitous ARP increases the risk of a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack.
questions.explanation: Gratuitous ARP lets hosts update ARP caches without being asked, which enables ARP poisoning and MITM on VoIP traffic.
optionNotes: Unrelated to VLAN 1
ARP is a layer 2 protocol, unrelated to L3
Not a brute-force vector
Correct: unsolicited ARP enables cache poisoning and MITM

questions.stem: Which of the following is MOST effective in detecting information hiding in Transmission Control Protocol/internet Protocol (TCP/IP) traffic?
questions.explanation: Application-level firewalls inspect payloads in depth and can spot covert data hidden in protocols.
optionNotes: Stateful inspection tracks connections, not payload content
Correct: deep application inspection reveals hidden data in protocols
Content filters target URLs/categories rather than covert channels
Header-only filtering cannot see hidden data

questions.stem: Within the company, desktop clients receive Internet Protocol (IP) address over Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). Which of the following represents a valid measure to help protect the network against unauthorized access?
options: Implement DHCP to assign IP address to server systems
questions.explanation: 802.1X port-based NAC stops unauthorized devices from getting network access.
optionNotes: Path management is unrelated to access
Correct: 802.1X authenticates devices before they get network access
Server addressing doesn't stop unauthorized clients
Change management is a process, not an access control

questions.stem: In a High Availability (HA) environment, what is the PRIMARY goal of working with a virtual router address as the gateway to a network?
options: The second of two routers can periodically check in to make sure that the first router is operational.
The second of two routers can better absorb a Denial of Service (DoS) attack knowing the first router is present.
The first of two routers fails and is reinstalled, while the second handles the traffic flawlessly.
The first of two routers can better handle specific traffic, while the second handles the rest of the traffic seamlessly.
questions.explanation: A virtual router address (VRRP/HSRP) allows transparent failover: if one router fails, the other carries traffic seamlessly.
optionNotes: Monitoring is the mechanism, not the goal
DoS absorption is not the purpose
Correct: seamless failover keeps the gateway available
That describes load sharing, not the primary HA goal

questions.stem: A security practitioner is tasked with securing the organization's Wireless Access Points (WAP). Which of these is the MOST effective way of restricting this environment to authorized users?
options: Enable Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) encryption on the wireless access point
Disable the broadcast of the Service Set Identifier (SSID) name
Change the name of the Service Set Identifier (SSID) to a random value not associated with the organization
Create Access Control Lists (ACL) based on Media Access Control (MAC) addresses
questions.explanation: WPA2 with strong authentication actually restricts access; SSID hiding and MAC filtering are easily bypassed.
optionNotes: Correct: WPA2 enforces authentication and encryption
SSID hiding is easily defeated
Renaming gives no real control
MAC addresses are easily spoofed

questions.stem: The MAIN use of Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) is to tunnel data
options: through a firewall at the Session layer
through a firewall at the Transport layer
questions.explanation: L2TP's main purpose is tunnelling PPP frames across an IP network.
optionNotes: L2TP is not a firewall traversal mechanism at the Session layer
L2TP is not a firewall traversal mechanism at the Transport layer
Correct: L2TP encapsulates PPP frames across IP networks
PCP compresses payloads; L2TP does not tunnel in it

questions.stem: Digital certificates used in Transport Layer Security (TLS) support which of the following?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said B] TLS server certificates authenticate the server and enable key exchange for confidential sessions; TLS does not provide non-repudiation.
optionNotes: Application function
TLS does not provide non-repudiation of messages
Not provided by certificates in TLS
Correct: server identity and confidentiality

questions.stem: "Stateful" differs from "Static" packet filtering firewalls by being aware of which of the following?
options: Difference between a new and an established connection
Difference between a malicious and a benign packet payload
questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls track connection state, distinguishing new from established sessions.
optionNotes: Correct: state tables let the firewall tell new connections from established ones
Static filters already see the source address in headers
Payload inspection is deep packet inspection/IPS, not statefulness
Tracking application sessions is an application proxy function

questions.stem: Transport Layer Security (TLS) provides which of the following capabilities for a remote access server?
questions.explanation: TLS authenticates peers using certificates and protects the session.
optionNotes: Compression is not a security capability and is deprecated in TLS
Application protocol negotiation (ALPN) is an extension, not the core service
Correct: TLS authenticates the peer via certificates
Revocation is handled by PKI mechanisms such as CRL/OCSP

questions.stem: In an organization where Network Access Control (NAC) has been deployed, a device trying to connect to the network is being placed into an isolated domain. What could be done on this device in order to obtain proper connectivity?
options: Connect the device to another network jack
Apply remediations according to security requirements
Change the Message Authentication Code (MAC) address of the network interface
questions.explanation: NAC quarantines non-compliant devices; remediating to meet policy restores access.
optionNotes: A different jack meets the same NAC check
Correct: meeting all compliance requirements releases quarantine
Patches may be only one of several requirements
Spoofing MAC is bypass, not proper connectivity

questions.stem: Extensible Authentication Protocol-Message Digest 5 (EAP-MD5) only provides which of the following?
questions.explanation: EAP-MD5 only provides one-way client authentication; no mutual auth or key material.
optionNotes: Mutual authentication needs methods like EAP-TLS/PEAP; MD5 lacks it
EAP-MD5 never authenticates the server
Correct: it is a one-way challenge-response of the user
EAP-MD5 produces no keys, so cannot encrypt data

questions.stem: What does a Synchronous (SYN) flood attack do?
options: Forces Transmission Control Protocol /Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) connections into a reset state
Establishes many new Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) connections
Empties the queue of pending Transmission Control Protocol /Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) requests
Exceeds the limits for new Transmission Control Protocol /Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) connections
questions.explanation: A SYN flood leaves half-open connections, exceeding the server's capacity for new connections.
optionNotes: Forcing resets is a TCP RST injection attack
Half-open connections are never fully established
It fills, not empties, the pending-connection queue
Correct: it exhausts the backlog for new connections

questions.stem: An organization has discovered that users are visiting unauthorized websites using anonymous proxies. Which of the following is the BEST way to prevent future occurrences?
options: Remove the anonymity from the proxy
Analyze Internet Protocol (IP) traffic for proxy requests
Disable the proxy server on the firewall
Block the Internet Protocol (IP) address of known anonymous proxies
questions.explanation: Blocking known anonymous proxy addresses prevents use.
optionNotes: The organization cannot control external anonymous proxies
Analysis detects but does not prevent
Disabling the company proxy does not stop external anonymous proxies
Correct: blocking known proxy IPs prevents connections to them

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective strategy to prevent an attacker from disabling a network?
options: Test business continuity and disaster recovery (DR) plans.
Design networks with the ability to adapt, reconfigure, and fail over.
Implement network segmentation to achieve robustness.
Follow security guidelines to prevent unauthorized network access.
questions.explanation: Resilient design that adapts and fails over keeps the network available despite attack. Resilience through redundancy and failover addresses availability directly, unlike controls that only limit access or aid recovery.
optionNotes: Testing BC/DR plans aids recovery but doesn't keep the network running.
Adaptive, failover-capable design keeps the network available under attack.
Segmentation limits spread but a segment can still be disabled.
Preventing unauthorized access doesn't stop external DoS.

questions.stem: An organization wants to share data securely with their partners via the Internet. Which standard port is typically used to meet this requirement?
options: Setup a server on User Datagram Protocol (UDP) port 69
Setup a server on Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) port 21
Setup a server on Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) port 22
Setup a server on Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) port 80
questions.explanation: TCP 22 (SSH/SFTP/SCP) provides encrypted file transfer. FTP, TFTP and HTTP all send data in cleartext.
optionNotes: UDP 69 is TFTP, unauthenticated and unencrypted.
TCP 21 is plain FTP, sends credentials in cleartext.
TCP 22 (SSH/SFTP) provides encrypted transfer.
TCP 80 is unencrypted HTTP.

questions.stem: What type of attack sends Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo requests to the target machine with a larger payload than the target can handle?
questions.explanation: Oversized ICMP echo (ping of death) is a DoS attack. The goal and effect is making the host unavailable.
optionNotes: MITM intercepts traffic; it doesn't flood oversized pings.
Ping of death (oversized ICMP echo) crashes the target: a DoS.
DNS poisoning corrupts name resolution.
An overflow is the mechanism exploited, but the attack class is DoS.

questions.stem: A hospital has allowed virtual private networking (VPN) access to remote database developers. Upon auditing the internal firewall configuration, the network administrator discovered that split-tunneling was enabled. What is the concern with this configuration?
options: Remote sessions will not require multi-layer authentication.
Remote clients are permitted to exchange traffic with the public and private network.
Multiple Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) tunnels may be exploitable in specific circumstances.
The network intrusion detection system (NIDS) will fail to inspect Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) traffic.
questions.explanation: Split tunneling lets the client talk to the internet and the private network simultaneously, bridging them. A compromised home network can then reach hospital systems through the client.
optionNotes: Split tunneling doesn't change authentication requirements.
The client is connected to the internet and the private network at once, bridging them.
Multiple tunnels aren't the concern of split tunneling.
SSL inspection by NIDS is unrelated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a standard Access Control List (ACL) element that enables a router to filter Internet traffic?
questions.explanation: Router ACLs filter on IP addresses. MAC addresses don't survive routing hops.
optionNotes: Routers don't filter internet traffic by MAC.
Standard ACLs filter on source IP address.
Roles aren't router ACL elements.
Not an ACL element.

questions.stem: Which of the following determines how traffic should flow based on the status of the infrastructure layer?
questions.explanation: The SDN control plane decides forwarding based on infrastructure state. It populates the forwarding tables that the data plane uses.
optionNotes: Not a standard SDN plane.
Application plane hosts apps requesting services.
Data plane forwards traffic.
Control plane decides forwarding using infrastructure state.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of Secure Shell (SSH)?
options: It operates at the network layer.
It encrypts transmitted User ID and passwords.
It uses challenge-response to authenticate each party.
It uses the International Data Encryption Algorithm (IDEA) for data privacy.
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts credentials, unlike Telnet. This replaces cleartext Telnet/rlogin.
optionNotes: SSH runs at application layer.
SSH encrypts credentials sent over the network.
SSH uses keys/passwords, not specifically challenge-response.
IDEA is not its standard cipher.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the GREATEST level of data security for a Virtual Private Network (VPN) connection?
questions.explanation: IPSec provides authentication, integrity and encryption of IP packets and is the standard protocol for securing VPN tunnels. The other options either only compress data or handle authentication, so they don't protect the data itself.
optionNotes: IPComp only compresses payloads; it provides no confidentiality or integrity.
Right: IPSec ESP/AH give encryption, integrity and origin authentication for tunnel traffic.
EAP is an authentication framework; it does not protect the data stream.
RADIUS provides AAA for remote users, not protection of VPN data.

questions.stem: Which of the following attacks, if successful, could give an intruder complete control of a software-defined networking (SDN) architecture?
options: Sniffing the traffic of a compromised host inside the network
Sending control messages to open a flow that does not pass a firewall from a compromised host within the network
A brute force password attack on the Secure Shell (SSH) port of the controller
Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) token replay attack
questions.explanation: The SDN controller is the centralised brain of the network; anyone who gains administrative access to it controls every flow. Brute-forcing the controller's SSH management interface would give exactly that access, while the other attacks affect only a single host or flow.
optionNotes: Sniffing from one host exposes local traffic only, not control of the architecture.
Opening one flow bypasses a firewall for that path but doesn't grant full control.
Right: compromising the controller's admin access gives complete control of SDN.
A RADIUS token replay might grant user access but not control of the controller.

questions.stem: What is the benefit of using Network Admission Control (NAC)?
options: Operating system (OS) versions can be validated prior to allowing network access.
NAC supports validation of the endpoint's security posture prior to allowing the session to go into an authorized state.
NAC can require the use of certificates, passwords, or a combination of both before allowing network admission.
NAC only supports Windows operating systems (OS).
questions.explanation: NAC checks an endpoint's security posture, such as patches, antivirus and configuration, before allowing it on the network, and quarantines or remediates devices that fail. This posture validation is NAC's defining benefit.
optionNotes: OS version is only one element of posture.
Right: NAC validates overall endpoint posture before authorizing access.
Authentication methods are supported but are not the defining benefit.
False: NAC supports many operating systems.

questions.stem: Secure real-time transport protocol (SRTP) provides security for which of the following?
options: Network Communication for real-time operating systems
questions.explanation: SRTP adds encryption, authentication and replay protection to RTP, the protocol that carries VoIP voice and video media streams. It is typically associated with voice communications.
optionNotes: Too vague; SRTP is specifically for RTP media streams.
Right: SRTP secures VoIP voice media.
Satellite links are not what SRTP targets.
SRTP is unrelated to real-time operating systems.

questions.stem: Utilizing a public wireless Local Area network (WLAN) to connect to a private network should be done only in which of the following situations?
options: Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is utilized to authenticate the user.
The client machine has a personal firewall and utilizes a Virtual Private Network (VPN) to connect to the network.
The client machine has antivirus software and has been scanned to determine if unauthorized ports are open.
The wireless Access Point (AP) is placed in the internal private network.
questions.explanation: Public Wi-Fi is untrusted, so the endpoint needs a host firewall against local attacks and a VPN to encrypt traffic to the private network. Together these give layered protection.
optionNotes: EAP authenticates the user but doesn't protect traffic on the open WLAN.
Right: a personal firewall plus VPN protects both the host and the traffic.
Antivirus and port scans don't protect data in transit.
Where the AP is placed has nothing to do with using a public WLAN.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the BEST mitigation practice for man-in-the-middle (MITM) Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) attacks?
questions.explanation: VoIP MITM attacks often target SIP signalling; protecting SIP with TLS (SIPS) authenticates endpoints and encrypts signalling, with SRTP covering the media. TLS is the applicable mitigation among the choices.
optionNotes: MGCP is a gateway control protocol with no inherent protection.
Right: TLS protects VoIP signalling against MITM.
FTP is unrelated and insecure.
SSH is not used for VoIP traffic.

questions.stem: A digitally-signed e-mail was delivered over a wireless network protected with Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol. Which of the following principles is at risk?
questions.explanation: A digital signature already provides integrity and non-repudiation, but it doesn't encrypt the message. WEP's weak encryption is easily broken, so the message's confidentiality is at risk.
optionNotes: WEP weakness doesn't directly threaten availability.
The signature preserves non-repudiation.
Right: the signed but unencrypted message is exposed by weak WEP.
The signature protects integrity.

questions.stem: A network security engineer needs to ensure that a security solution analyzes traffic for protocol manipulation and various sorts of common attacks. In addition, all Uniform Resource Locator (URL) traffic must be inspected and users prevented from browsing inappropriate websites. Which of the following solutions should be implemented to enable administrators the capability to analyze traffic, blacklist external sites, and log user traffic for later analysis?
questions.explanation: An application-level proxy understands HTTP, so it can inspect URLs, block categories of sites, detect protocol abuse and log user activity. A circuit-level proxy only sees session setup, and an IDS alerts without blocking browsing.
optionNotes: Detects but does not filter URLs or block sites
Works at session level; cannot inspect URLs
Correct: inspects application content, filters and logs URLs
Protects one host only

questions.stem: Which of the following was developed to support multiple protocols as well as provide login, password, and error correction capabilities?
questions.explanation: PPP supports multiple network protocols and provides authentication and error detection over serial links. CHAP and PAP are only authentication protocols used within PPP, and POP is for retrieving email.
optionNotes: Authentication protocol only
Correct
Cleartext authentication only
Mail retrieval

questions.stem: Which layer handle packet fragmentation and reassembly in the Open system interconnection (OSI) Reference model?
questions.explanation: In the OSI model the network layer handles fragmentation and reassembly of packets. IP fragments datagrams to fit the path MTU and reassembles them at the destination; the opt4 'datagrams' question asks something different.
optionNotes: Manages dialogs
Segments streams, not packet fragmentation
Frames on a local link
Correct: IP fragments and reassembles packets

questions.stem: Which of the following would need to be configured to ensure a device with a specific MAC address is always assigned the same IP address from DHCP?
questions.explanation: A DHCP reservation binds a MAC address to a fixed IP. Exclusions remove addresses from the pool, and static assignment is configured on the client rather than in DHCP.
optionNotes: Options such as gateway and DNS, not a binding
Correct: MAC-to-IP reservation
Random from the pool
Removes addresses from the pool
Set on the host, not in DHCP

questions.stem: Configuring a Wireless Access Point (WAP) with the same Service Set Identifier (SSID) as another WAP in order to have users unknowingly connect is referred to as which of the following?
questions.explanation: An attacker who stands up an access point broadcasting a legitimate SSID (an evil twin) lures clients into associating with it. All their traffic then passes through the attacker, who can read or alter it, which is a man-in-the-middle position.
optionNotes: Jamming floods the RF band to deny service; it does not impersonate a network
Right: the evil twin inserts the attacker between victims and the real network
War driving only discovers wireless networks while moving around
IP spoofing forges layer-3 source addresses and has nothing to do with SSIDs

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason a sniffer operating on a network is collecting packets only from its own host?
options: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) has dropped the packets.
The network is connected using switches.
The network is connected using hubs.
The network's firewall does not allow sniffing.
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said A] A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards unicast frames only out of the destination port. A sniffer on an ordinary switch port therefore sees its own traffic plus broadcasts, unless port mirroring or ARP poisoning is used.
optionNotes: An IDS monitors traffic; it does not selectively drop frames to hide them from sniffers
Right: switching isolates each port's unicast traffic
Hubs repeat every frame to every port, so the sniffer would see everyone's packets
Perimeter firewalls do not control local promiscuous-mode capture on a LAN segment

questions.stem: Which of the following needs to be tested to achieve a Cat 6a certification for a company's data cabling?
questions.explanation: Category 6a certification tests the permanent link or channel, which typically runs from the patch panel to the wall outlet. The patch panel terminations are therefore part of what is tested against the TIA performance limits.
optionNotes: RJ11 is a telephone connector and is not part of Cat 6a data cabling
LC connectors terminate fibre, not twisted pair
Right: patch panel terminations are part of the tested link
F-type connectors are for coaxial cable

questions.stem: To monitor the security of buried data lines inside the perimeter of a facility, which of the following is the MOST effective control?
options: Fencing around the facility with closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at all entry points
Ground sensors installed and reporting to a security event management (SEM) system
Steel casing around the facility ingress points
regular sweeps of the perimeter, including manual inspection of the cable ingress points
questions.explanation: Buried cables are best monitored by sensors that detect ground disturbance such as digging or vibration along the cable route. Feeding these alerts into a monitoring system gives continuous detection.
optionNotes: Fences and entry-point CCTV do not watch the buried cable route
Right: continuous ground sensing reports tampering in real time
Steel casing protects only the ingress points and does not detect anything
Periodic manual sweeps leave long gaps between checks

questions.stem: A network administrator is configuring a database server and would like to ensure the database engine is listening on a certain port. Which of the following commands should the administrator use to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: netstat -a lists all active connections and listening TCP/UDP ports. It confirms whether the database engine is listening on the expected port.
optionNotes: nslookup queries DNS records
Right: shows listening ports
ipconfig shows interface addressing, not listening ports
arp -a shows the IP-to-MAC cache

questions.stem: When telephones in a city are connected by a single exchange, the caller can only connect with the switchboard operator. The operator then manually connects the call. This is an example of which type of network topology?
questions.explanation: Every phone line runs to a single central switchboard that makes every connection. A central hub with individual spokes is a star topology.
optionNotes: Right: a central exchange with spokes is a star
A tree is a hierarchy of linked stars; here there is only one exchange
PPP is a link-layer protocol, not a topology
A bus uses one shared cable with no central switching point

questions.stem: When configuring Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) in a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) network, which of the following authentication types is the MOST secure?
questions.explanation: EAP-TLS uses mutual certificate authentication and is the strongest EAP method. Client-side certificates remove password-based attack paths.
optionNotes: Mutual certificate-based authentication; strongest EAP method.
EAP-FAST uses PACs and is weaker than mutual certificates.
EAP-TTLS needs only a server certificate; the inner client auth is weaker.
PEAP needs only a server certificate plus an inner password method.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct feature of a virtual local area network (VLAN)?
options: A VLAN segregates network traffic therefore information security is enhanced significantly.
Layer 3 routing is required to allow traffic from one VLAN to another.
VLAN has certain security features such as where the devices are physically connected.
There is no broadcast allowed within a single VLAN due to network segregation.
questions.explanation: Inter-VLAN traffic needs Layer 3 routing. A VLAN is a single broadcast domain.
optionNotes: VLANs are not strong security boundaries; VLAN hopping exists.
Inter-VLAN traffic requires Layer 3 routing.
VLANs are logical, independent of physical connection.
Broadcasts do occur within a VLAN; the VLAN is a broadcast domain.

questions.stem: Which of the following uses the destination IP address to forward packets?
questions.explanation: Routers forward at Layer 3 using destination IP addresses. Layer 3 equals IP addressing.
optionNotes: Bridges forward on MAC addresses.
Layer 2 switches use MAC addresses.
Routers forward on destination IP.
Repeaters regenerate signals only.

questions.stem: Wireless users are reporting intermittent Internet connectivity. Connectivity is restored when the users disconnect and reconnect, utilizing the web authentication process each time. The network administrator can see the devices connected to the APs at all times. Which of the following steps will MOST likely determine the cause of the issue?
options: Verify the session time-out configuration on the captive portal settings
Check for encryption protocol mismatch on the client's wireless settings.
Confirm that a valid passphrase is being used during the web authentication.
Investigate for a client's disassociation caused by an evil twin AP
questions.explanation: Users stay associated but lose access until re-authenticating: a captive portal session timeout. Devices stay associated, so the problem is above Layer 2.
optionNotes: A session timeout on the captive portal explains drops fixed by re-authentication.
An encryption mismatch would prevent association entirely.
An invalid passphrase would fail authentication outright.
An evil twin would disassociate clients, but APs show them connected.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of datacenter architectures will MOST likely be used in a large SDN and can be extended beyond the datacenter?
questions.explanation: Spine-and-leaf is the flat, scalable fabric that software-defined data centres use: every leaf switch connects to every spine, giving predictable east-west paths that an SDN controller can program and that can be stretched across sites with overlays such as VXLAN. A classic three-tier design is the older hierarchy it replaces, and top-of-rack is only a cabling/placement choice inside a rack.
optionNotes: Wrong: iSCSI is a storage protocol, not a data centre architecture.
Wrong: FCoE carries Fibre Channel storage traffic over Ethernet; it is not a fabric design.
Wrong: the traditional core/aggregation/access hierarchy scales poorly for east-west SDN traffic.
Right: a scalable leaf-spine fabric suited to large SDN deployments and extendable with overlays.
Wrong: top-of-rack describes where access switches sit, not the overall architecture.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the use of network architecture in reducing corporate risks associated with mobile devices?
options: Maintaining a "closed applications" model on all mobile devices depends on demilitarized zone (DMZ) servers
Split tunneling enabled for mobile devices improves demilitarized zone (DMZ) security posture
Segmentation and demilitarized zone (DMZ) monitoring are implemented to secure a virtual private network (VPN) access for mobile devices
Applications that manage mobile devices are located in an Internet demilitarized zone (DMZ)
questions.explanation: Segmenting the network and monitoring the DMZ through which mobile VPN access terminates is the architectural measure that reduces mobile-device risk. It contains mobile traffic and gives visibility before it reaches internal assets.
optionNotes: Closed app model is device policy, not network architecture
Split tunneling increases risk
Right: segmentation plus DMZ monitoring protects mobile VPN access
Placing MDM in an Internet DMZ is a deployment detail, not risk reduction

questions.stem: Which of the following MOST applies to Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) security?
options: It leverages Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) over Transport Layer Security (TLS).
It requires a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI).
It reuses security mechanisms derived from existing protocols.
questions.explanation: SIP does not define its own security; it reuses mechanisms from existing protocols such as TLS, S/MIME and HTTP digest authentication.
optionNotes: SIP uses its own transport, not HTTP over TLS
PKI is not required
Right: SIP does not define its own security; it reuses mechanisms from existing protocols such as TLS, S/MIME and HTTP digest authentication.
SIP lacks native end-to-end security

questions.stem: During a recent assessment an organization has discovered that the wireless signal can be detected outside the campus area. What logical control should be implemented in order to BEST protect the confidentiality of information traveling over the wireless transmission media?
options: Configure a firewall to logically separate the data at the boundary.
Configure the Access Points (AP) to use Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) encryption.
Disable the Service Set Identifier (SSID) broadcast on the Access Points (AP).
Perform regular technical assessments on the Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN).
questions.explanation: Confidentiality of data over the air requires encryption; WPA2 encrypts wireless traffic so intercepted signals are unreadable.
optionNotes: Firewall does not protect over-the-air traffic
Right: Confidentiality of data over the air requires encryption; WPA2 encrypts wireless traffic so intercepted signals are unreadable.
Hiding SSID is weak obscurity
Assessments do not protect data

questions.stem: Two computers, each with a single connection on the same physical 10 gigabit Ethernet network segment, need to communicate with each other. The first machine has a single Internet Protocol (IP) Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) address of 192.168.1.3/30 and the second machine has an IP/CIDR address 192.168.1.6/30. Which of the following is correct?
options: Since each computer is on a different layer 3 network, traffic between the computers must be processed by a network bridge in order to communicate.
Since each computer is on the same layer 3 network, traffic between the computers may be processed by a network bridge in order to communicate.
Since each computer is on the same layer 3 network, traffic between the computers may be processed by a network router in order to communicate.
Since each computer is on a different layer 3 network, traffic between the computers must be processed by a network router in order to communicate.
questions.explanation: A /30 has 4 addresses: .3 is in 192.168.1.0/30 and .6 in 192.168.1.4/30, separate layer 3 networks, so a router is required.
optionNotes: Bridges are layer 2
They are not on the same network
They are not on the same network
Right: A /30 has 4 addresses:.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective way to ensure the endpoint devices used by remote users are compliant with an organization's approved policies before being allowed on the network?
questions.explanation: NAC checks endpoint posture against policy before admitting it to the network.
optionNotes: GPO applies settings to domain members only
Right: NAC checks endpoint posture against policy before admitting it to the network.
MDM manages mobile devices but doesn't gate network admission
PAM manages privileged accounts

questions.stem: Which of the following types of firewall only examines the "handshaking" between packets before forwarding traffic?
questions.explanation: Circuit-level gateways (e.g., SOCKS) work at the session layer and only validate the TCP handshake/session setup; once the circuit is established, packets pass without content inspection.
optionNotes: Proxy (application-level) firewalls inspect application content, not just the handshake.
Host-based firewalls describe placement, not an inspection method.
Correct: circuit-level firewalls only verify session establishment (handshake).
NAT translates addresses; it is not an inspection technique.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of devices can provide content filtering and threat protection, and manage multiple IPSec site-to-site connections?
questions.explanation: A next-generation firewall combines stateful filtering with content/URL filtering, IPS-style threat protection and VPN termination, so one device covers all three needs. The other devices only satisfy part of the requirement.
optionNotes: Layer 3 switch routes but does no content filtering or IPsec management.
VPN headend terminates tunnels but lacks content filtering/threat protection.
Correct: NGFW does content filtering, threat protection and site-to-site IPsec.
Proxy server filters content but does not manage IPsec site-to-site tunnels.
IPS provides threat protection only, no VPN or content filtering.

questions.stem: Which of the following actions MUST be performed when using secure multipurpose internet mail Extension (S/MIME) before sending an encrypted message to a recipient?
questions.explanation: To encrypt for a recipient in S/MIME the sender needs the recipient's public key, obtained from the recipient's certificate.
optionNotes: Signing is optional and not required for encryption.
Private keys are never shared.
Correct: the certificate supplies the recipient's public key.
Attachments are encrypted as part of the message, not a prerequisite.

questions.stem: In a multi-tenant cloud environment, what approach will secure logical access to assets?
questions.explanation: A VPC logically isolates a tenant's resources inside a shared public cloud.
optionNotes: Wrong: A deployment model, not isolation
Wrong: Detective oversight, not isolation
Wrong: Configuration control does not separate tenants
Right: a VPC isolates one tenant's network logically

questions.stem: Which Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer(s) BEST corresponds to the network access layer in the Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) model?
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP network access (link) layer corresponds to OSI Physical and Data Link.
optionNotes: Wrong: Maps to TCP/IP transport
Right: network access = OSI Physical + Data Link
Wrong: Maps to TCP/IP application
Wrong: Mismatched layers

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered the PRIMARY security issue associated with encrypted e-mail messages?
options: Scanning for viruses and other malware
Greater costs associated for backups and restores
questions.explanation: Encrypted email depends on exchanging and managing keys between correspondents, which is its main difficulty.
optionNotes: Right: exchanging keys securely is the main hurdle
Wrong: Not specific to encryption
Wrong: A real but secondary issue
Wrong: Minor

questions.stem: An information technology (IT) employee who travels frequently to various locations connects remotely to an organization's systems to troubleshoot problems. Which of the following solutions BEST serves as a secure control mechanism to meet the organization's requirements?
options: Update the firewall rules to include the static Internet Protocol (IP) addresses of the locations where the employee connects from.
Install a third-party screen sharing solution that provides remote connection from a public website.
Implement a Dynamic Domain Name Services (DDNS) account to initiate a virtual private network (VPN) using the DDNS record.
Install a bastion host in the demilitarized zone (DMZ) and allow multi-factor authentication (MFA) access.
questions.explanation: A hardened bastion host in the DMZ with MFA gives secure remote access from changing locations.
optionNotes: Wrong: The employee's IPs change
Wrong: A public third-party tool is risky
Wrong: DDNS adds no authentication
Right: a hardened DMZ access point with strong authentication
