questions.stem: What is a security concern when considering implementing software-defined networking (SDN)?
questions.explanation: The centralized controller and programmable interfaces add new targets, enlarging the attack surface.
optionNotes: Right: the controller and APIs become new targets
Wrong: Not inherently a concern
Wrong: SDN is centralized
Wrong: Not necessarily cloud

questions.stem: Which layer of the Open system Interconnect (OSI) model is responsible for secure data transfer between applications, flow control, and error detection and correction?
questions.explanation: The transport layer (Layer 4) handles end-to-end delivery, flow control and error recovery.
optionNotes: Wrong: Data link
Right: the transport layer handles reliability and flow control
Wrong: Session
Wrong: Presentation

questions.stem: Which of the following is a peer entity authentication method for Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP)?
questions.explanation: CHAP is PPP's challenge-response peer authentication protocol, verifying the peer with a hashed shared secret without sending it in clear.
optionNotes: Correct: CHAP is PPP's challenge-response peer authentication protocol
MAC protects message integrity; it is not a PPP authentication protocol
TLS handshake is not how PPP authenticates its peer
Too generic: describes a technique, not the named PPP protocol

questions.stem: Which of the following is a PRIMARY security weakness in the design of Domain Name System (DNS)?
options: A DNS server can be disabled in a denial-of-service (DoS) attack.
A DNS server does not authenticate source of information.
Each DNS server must hold the address of the root servers.
A DNS server database can be injected with falsified checksums.
questions.explanation: Classic DNS has no mechanism to authenticate the origin or integrity of responses, which enables spoofing and cache poisoning; DNSSEC was created to fix this.
optionNotes: DoS is a risk to any service, not a DNS design flaw
Correct: no origin authentication, which allows spoofing and cache poisoning
Knowing the root hints is a normal operational need, not a weakness
DNS does not use checksums in this way; the option is a distractor

questions.stem: How can a security engineer maintain network separation from a secure environment while allowing remote users to work in the secure environment?
options: Use a Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) to segment the network
Enforce port security on access switches
questions.explanation: A hardened bastion host acts as the controlled entry point for remote users into the secure environment, keeping the networks separated.
optionNotes: A VLAN gives logical segmentation but no controlled remote entry point
Correct: a hardened gateway mediates remote access while preserving separation
Antivirus does not provide network separation
Port security limits local switch ports, not remote access

questions.stem: Which of the following is included in the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) security framework?
questions.explanation: GSM security uses symmetric algorithms (A3/A5/A8) with a secret key Ki shared between the SIM and the network; it does not use PKI.
optionNotes: GSM does not use PKI
Correct: A3/A5/A8 use the shared secret Ki
GSM does not use digital signatures
Biometrics are not part of GSM

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)?
options: Maintain a list of network paths between internet routers.
Provide Routing Information Protocol (RIP) version 2 advertisements to neighboring layer 3 devices.
Provide firewall services to cloud-enabled applications.
Maintain a list of efficient network paths between autonomous systems.
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol that exchanges and selects routes between autonomous systems.
optionNotes: Too vague: BGP routes between ASes, not between arbitrary routers
BGP is not related to RIP
BGP is not a firewall
Correct: path selection between autonomous systems

questions.stem: A new site's gateway isn't able to form a tunnel to the existing site-to-site Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) virtual private network (VPN) device at headquarters. Devices at the new site have no problem accessing resources on the Internet. When testing connectivity between the remote site's gateway, it was observed that the external Internet Protocol (IP) address of the gateway was set to 192.168.1.1 and was configured to send outbound traffic to the Internet Service Provider (ISP) gateway at 192.168.1.2. Which of the following would be the BEST way to resolve the issue and get the remote site connected?
options: Enable IPSec tunnel mode on the VPN devices at the new site and the corporate headquarters.
Enable Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) on the VPN devices at the new site and the corporate headquarters.
Enable Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP) on the VPN devices at the new site and the corporate headquarters.
Enable Network Address Translation (NAT) - Traversal on the VPN devices at the new site and the corporate headquarters.
questions.explanation: The gateway sits behind NAT (it has a private address), and NAT breaks IPsec AH/ESP; enabling NAT-Traversal encapsulates IPsec in UDP 4500 so the tunnel can form.
optionNotes: Tunnel mode is already standard for site-to-site; it is not the NAT fix
L2TP does not solve NAT traversal
PPTP is insecure and irrelevant here
Correct: NAT-T encapsulates IPsec in UDP 4500

questions.stem: Compared to a traditional network, which of the following is a security-related benefit that software-defined networking (SDN) provides?
questions.explanation: SDN separates the control plane into a centralized controller, giving administrators unified control to enforce security policy consistently.
optionNotes: Provisioning is an operational benefit, less security-focused
Correct: centralized control gives consistent policy enforcement
Latency is not a security benefit
Cost is not a security benefit

questions.stem: What method could be used to prevent passive attacks against secure voice communications between an organization and its vendor?
questions.explanation: Passive attacks such as eavesdropping capture data as it crosses the network, so the defence is to encrypt the voice stream in transit (e.g., SRTP). Encryption makes intercepted traffic unintelligible regardless of the path it takes.
optionNotes: Correct: encrypting the voice stream in transit defeats eavesdropping.
A VPN is only one way to get encryption in transit; the general control is encryption itself.
A dedicated line is still physically tappable unless it is encrypted.
Encryption at rest protects stored data, not live voice traffic.

questions.stem: Which software defined networking (SDN) architectural component is responsible for translating network requirements?
questions.explanation: In SDN the controller sits in the control plane. It takes the requirements that applications send over the northbound interface and turns them into forwarding instructions for the data path via southbound protocols.
optionNotes: Applications state the requirements; they don't translate them.
The data path only forwards packets according to the rules it is given.
Correct: the controller translates application requirements into data-plane rules.
The northbound interface is the channel the requirements travel over, not the translator.

questions.stem: Recently, an unknown event has disrupted a single Layer-2 network that spans between two geographically diverse data centers. The network engineers have asked for assistance in identifying the root cause of the event. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Stretching one Layer-2 network across two data centres creates a very large broadcast and failure domain. Broadcast storms or spanning-tree problems then spread across both sites, which explains an unexplained disruption.
optionNotes: Routing protocols run at Layer 3; this is a single Layer-2 segment.
A Smurf attack is possible but is not the MOST likely root cause.
Correct: an oversized stretched broadcast domain amplifies storms and STP failures.
Spoofing is less likely than the architectural problem.

questions.stem: Which of the following protocols will allow the encrypted transfer of content on the Internet?
questions.explanation: Secure copy (SCP) runs over SSH, so file content is encrypted in transit. SMB, HTTP and rcp send it in cleartext by default.
optionNotes: SMB is not encrypted by default.
Correct: SCP uses SSH encryption.
HTTP is cleartext.
rcp is cleartext.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of hosts should be operating in the demilitarized zone (DMZ)?
options: Hosts intended to provide limited access to public resources
Database servers that can provide useful information to the public
Hosts that store unimportant data such as demographical information
questions.explanation: The DMZ hosts public-facing services that give limited access to resources meant for outsiders. Internal data stays behind the inner firewall.
optionNotes: Correct: public-facing hosts with limited access.
Database servers belong on the internal network.
Even 'unimportant' data stores don't belong there.
File servers with organisational data belong internally.

questions.stem: A criminal organization is planning an attack on a government network. Which of the following scenarios presents the HIGHEST risk to the organization?
options: Network is flooded with communication traffic by the attacker.
Organization loses control of their network devices.
Attacker accesses sensitive information regarding the network topology.
questions.explanation: If the organisation loses control of its network devices, the attacker effectively owns the infrastructure and can cause any of the other outcomes. Flooding and disrupted management traffic are usually temporary availability problems. Topology information only helps the attacker prepare.
optionNotes: A flood hurts availability, but is usually temporary and recoverable.
Correct: losing device control is total compromise, the highest risk.
Disrupted management traffic is serious, but less than losing control.
Topology information is reconnaissance; it does no damage by itself.

questions.stem: An organization wants to migrate to Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) to save on telephony expenses. Which of the following security related statements should be considered in the decision-making process?
options: Cloud telephony is less secure and more expensive than digital telephony services.
SIP services are more secure when used with multi-layer security proxies.
H.323 media gateways must be used to ensure end-to-end security tunnels.
Given the behavior of SIP traffic, additional security controls would be required.
questions.explanation: SIP signalling opens media ports dynamically and is open to eavesdropping, toll fraud and denial of service. Moving to it means adding controls such as session border controllers, TLS/SRTP and separate voice VLANs. The other statements are false or too absolute.
optionNotes: A sweeping, unsupported generalisation.
Proxies help, but the statement is narrow and not the key consideration.
H.323 is a different protocol and is not needed for SIP security.
Correct: SIP's behaviour requires additional security controls.

questions.stem: What are the three key benefits that application developers should derive from the northbound application-programming interface (API) of software-defined networking (SDN)?
options: Familiar syntax, abstraction of network topology, and definition of network protocols
Network syntax, abstraction of network flow, and abstraction of network protocols
Network syntax, abstraction of network commands, and abstraction of network protocols
Familiar syntax, abstraction of network topology, and abstraction of network protocols
questions.explanation: The SDN northbound API lets applications program the network using familiar syntax, without knowing the network's topology or protocol details. Developers write against an abstraction instead of defining protocols or using device-level syntax.
optionNotes: Developers do not define network protocols; those are abstracted away.
'Network syntax' is what the API hides from developers.
Same problem: it relies on network syntax.
Correct: familiar syntax plus abstraction of topology and protocols.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the MOST secure method for Network Access Control (NAC)?
questions.explanation: 802.1X authenticates a device or user before the switch port or wireless association is opened. That makes it the strongest NAC mechanism listed. MAC addresses are easy to spoof, and NAT and application filtering are not access-control mechanisms for the network.
optionNotes: MAC addresses are trivially spoofed.
Correct: 802.1X provides authenticated port-based NAC.
Filters traffic content; it does not control network admission.
NAT translates addresses; it is not access control.

questions.stem: Why might a network administrator choose distributed virtual switches instead of stand-alone switches for network segmentation?
options: To standardize on a single vendor
To ensure isolation of management traffic
To reduce the risk of configuration errors
questions.explanation: A distributed virtual switch is configured once centrally and applied across all hypervisor hosts. Segmentation settings then stay consistent and configuration errors become less likely. Vendor choice and data-plane efficiency are not the reasons.
optionNotes: Vendor standardisation is not the security reason.
Management traffic can be isolated on either kind of switch.
Efficiency is not the main advantage.
Correct: central configuration reduces configuration errors.

questions.stem: Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) provides users with a higher level of assurance that their data will remain protected by using which protocol?
questions.explanation: WPA2-Enterprise uses 802.1X with EAP for strong mutual authentication. With AES-CCMP, that gives better assurance than earlier schemes. SSH, IPsec and SSL are not part of WPA2.
optionNotes: SSH secures remote shells, not Wi-Fi.
IPsec is a network-layer VPN and not part of WPA2.
SSL/TLS is used inside some EAP methods, not by WPA2 directly.
Correct: WPA2-Enterprise authenticates through EAP.

questions.stem: Which of the following routing protocols is used to exchange route information between public autonomous systems?
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol used to exchange routes between autonomous systems on the internet. OSPF, EIGRP and RIP are interior gateway protocols.
optionNotes: OSPF is an interior protocol.
Correct: BGP exchanges routes between autonomous systems.
EIGRP is an interior protocol from Cisco.
RIP is an interior distance-vector protocol.

questions.stem: Two remote offices need to be connected securely over an untrustworthy MAN. Each office needs to access network shares at the other site. Which of the following will BEST provide this functionality?
questions.explanation: A site-to-site VPN builds a permanent encrypted tunnel between the two offices' gateways, letting each reach the other's file shares across the untrusted MAN. Client VPNs are for individual users, and split tunnelling is a client setting.
optionNotes: Client-to-site serves individual remote users, not whole offices.
A third-party service adds trust dependencies and is not needed.
Correct: site-to-site connects the two networks securely.
Split tunnelling is a client routing option.

questions.stem: The Secure Shell (SSH) version 2 protocol supports.
questions.explanation: SSH-2 provides server/user authentication, compression, encryption for confidentiality, and MAC-based integrity.
optionNotes: Availability and accountability are not SSH services.
Availability is not provided by SSH.
Accountability is not an SSH protocol feature.
Correct: SSH-2 offers authentication, compression, encryption, MAC integrity.

questions.stem: Why are packet filtering routers used in low-risk environments?
options: They are high-resolution source discrimination and identification tools.
They are fast and flexible, and protect against Internet Protocol (IP) spoofing.
They are fast, flexible, and transparent.
They enforce strong user authentication and audit log generation.
questions.explanation: Packet filters are fast, flexible and transparent but weak, suiting low-risk settings.
optionNotes: Packet filters cannot strongly identify sources.
They do not protect against IP spoofing well.
Correct: speed, flexibility and transparency suit low-risk needs.
They provide no user authentication.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN difference between a network-based firewall and a host-based firewall?
options: A network-based firewall is stateful, while a host-based firewall is stateless.
A network-based firewall controls traffic passing through the device, while a host-based firewall controls traffic destined for the device.
A network-based firewall verifies network traffic, while a host-based firewall verifies processes and applications.
A network-based firewall blocks network intrusions, while a host-based firewall blocks malware.
questions.explanation: Network firewalls filter traffic traversing the device; host firewalls filter traffic to/from the host itself.
optionNotes: Both can be stateful.
Correct: network firewall filters transit traffic; host firewall filters its own traffic.
Both filter network traffic; app awareness isn't the main difference.
Neither is defined by malware blocking.

questions.stem: At the destination host, which of the following OSI model layers will discard a segment with a bad checksum in the UDP header?
questions.explanation: The UDP checksum is checked by the transport layer, which discards bad segments.
optionNotes: Network layer checks IP header, not UDP.
Data link checks frame CRC, not UDP checksum.
Correct: UDP checksum is verified at transport.
Session layer doesn't process UDP checksums.

questions.stem: An access control list (ACL) on a router is a feature MOST similar to which type of firewall?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] Router ACLs permit/deny packets on addresses/ports, the defining trait of packet-filtering firewalls.
optionNotes: Correct: ACLs filter per packet on header fields.
Application gateways inspect application data.
Heuristic firewalls analyse behaviour.
Basic ACLs don't track connection state.

questions.stem: Which layer of the Open systems Interconnection (OSI) model is being targeted in the event of a Synchronization (SYN) flood attack?
questions.explanation: SYN flood abuses the TCP handshake at the transport layer.
optionNotes: Session layer isn't where TCP handshake runs.
Correct: SYN flood abuses TCP at transport.
Network layer handles IP routing.
Presentation layer handles format/encryption.

questions.stem: Which Wide Area Network (WAN) technology requires the first router in the path to determine the full path the packet will travel, removing the need for other routers in the path to make independent determinations?
questions.explanation: MPLS assigns labels at the ingress router, which fixes the label-switched path so downstream routers just switch on labels rather than making their own routing decisions.
optionNotes: Right: ingress label edge router sets the path
Optical transport, no path determination
VoIP signaling protocol
Storage protocol over Ethernet

questions.stem: Which of the following attack types can be used to compromise the integrity of data during transmission?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said B] Session hijacking lets an attacker take over an established session and inject or alter traffic, which attacks integrity. Packet sniffing is passive and threatens confidentiality, not integrity.
optionNotes: Captures keystrokes at the endpoint; confidentiality
Passive capture; confidentiality
SYN flood attacks availability
Right: active takeover allows tampering with data in transit

questions.stem: Why would a security architect specify that a default route pointing to a sinkhole be injected into internal networks?
options: To have firewalls route all network traffic
To detect the traffic destined to non-existent network destinations
To exercise authority over the network department
To re-inject the route into external networks
questions.explanation: A default route to a sinkhole draws traffic sent to destinations with no real route, so it can be logged and analyzed, which exposes scanning, malware beaconing and misconfigurations.
optionNotes: Firewalls do not need this
Not a technical purpose
Right: detects traffic to non-existent destinations
Leaking internal routes outward would be harmful

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common measure within a Local Area Network (LAN) to provide an additional level of security through segmentation?
questions.explanation: VLANs logically segment a LAN into separate broadcast domains.
optionNotes: Right: LAN segmentation
DMZ separates internal from external, not LAN segmentation
Malware control
Detection, not segmentation

questions.stem: An information security administrator wishes to block peer-to-peer (P2P) traffic over Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) tunnels. Which of the following layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model requires inspection?
questions.explanation: P2P carried inside HTTP is only visible by looking at application payloads, so Layer 7 inspection is needed.
optionNotes: Formatting/encryption layer
Ports alone show HTTP
Session management only
Right: payload inspection

questions.stem: A network administrator is designing a new datacenter in a different region that will need to communicate to the old datacenter with a secure connection. Which of the following access methods would provide the BEST security for this new datacenter?
questions.explanation: A site-to-site VPN securely links two networks over an untrusted network, which is exactly what datacenter-to-datacenter connectivity needs.
optionNotes: Remote desktop tool
Host-level admin access
Not a secure inter-site method
Right: encrypted network-to-network tunnel

questions.stem: An IT technician suspects a break in one of the uplinks that provides connectivity to the core switch. Which of the following command-line tools should the technician use to determine where the incident is occurring?
questions.explanation: 'show interface' shows link status, errors and up/down state per port, which pinpoints a broken uplink.
optionNotes: DNS lookup
Shows configuration, not link state
Host connection list
Right: per-interface status
Counters alone are less direct

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE about Secure Shell (SSH)?
options: SSH does not protect against man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.
SSH supports port forwarding, which can be used to protect less secured protocols.
SSH can be used with almost any application because it is concerned with maintaining a circuit.
SSH is easy to deploy because it requires a Web browser only.
questions.explanation: SSH supports port forwarding (tunneling), which can wrap insecure protocols in an encrypted channel.
optionNotes: Host keys protect against MITM
Right: tunneling
Describes circuit-level proxies like SOCKS
Needs an SSH client, not just a browser

questions.stem: Additional padding may be added to the Encapsulating Security Protocol (ESP) trailer to provide which of the following?
questions.explanation: ESP padding can hide the true length of the payload, which gives partial traffic-flow confidentiality.
optionNotes: Not padding's role
Right: hides payload length
Sequence numbers do this
Integrity/authentication does this

questions.stem: When conducting a remote access session using Internet Protocol Security (IPSec), which Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model layer does this connection use?
questions.explanation: IPsec works at the Network layer (Layer 3), protecting IP packets, which is why it can carry any upper-layer protocol in a remote-access tunnel.
optionNotes: TLS/SSL sits higher; IPsec is below Transport.
Correct: IPsec is a Layer 3 protocol suite.
L2TP/PPTP-style framing is Layer 2, not IPsec.
Presentation handles data formatting, not IPsec.

questions.stem: Which of the following protection is provided when using a Virtual Private Network (VPN) with Authentication Header (AH)?
questions.explanation: AH provides data origin authentication and integrity (plus anti-replay), but no encryption. Of the choices, origin authentication, framed here as sender non-repudiation, is the only property AH offers. Strictly, its symmetric keys give authentication rather than true non-repudiation.
optionNotes: AH does not encrypt; ESP does.
AH provides no confidentiality.
Correct: AH authenticates the sender and packet integrity.
AH is packet authentication, not user MFA.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques is effective to detect taps in fiber optic cables?
options: Taking baseline signal level of the cable
Measuring signal through external oscillator solution devices
questions.explanation: Tapping a fiber causes measurable optical loss. Recording a baseline signal level (for example with an OTDR) and watching for drops reveals taps. Fiber emits no EM field, and vulnerability scanning cannot see physical taps.
optionNotes: Correct: deviation from baseline signal loss indicates a tap.
Not a recognised fiber-tap detection method.
Fiber carries light and emits no EM field to measure.
Scanning finds software flaws, not physical taps.

questions.stem: If the wide area network (WAN) is supporting converged applications like Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), which of the following becomes even MORE essential to the assurance of network?
questions.explanation: VoIP needs predictable latency and jitter. Deterministic routing gives consistent, known paths so real-time traffic gets reliable quality across the WAN.
optionNotes: CIDR is an addressing efficiency scheme.
Correct: predictable paths support real-time voice QoS.
Route lookups are generic to all IP traffic.
Boundary routing relates to edges, not voice assurance.

questions.stem: Which is MOST important when negotiating an Internet service provider (ISP) service-level agreement (SLA) by an organization that solely provides Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services?
options: Financial penalties in case of disruption
questions.explanation: For a business that only sells VoIP, call quality depends on latency, jitter and loss guarantees, so QoS is the key SLA term. Availability alone does not make voice usable.
optionNotes: MTTR matters after outages, but voice quality is ongoing.
Correct: QoS guarantees determine voice quality.
Needed, but not sufficient for voice.
Penalties compensate; they do not ensure service.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce the impact of an externally sourced flood attack?
options: Block the source address at the firewall.
Have this service provider block the source address.
Block all inbound traffic until the flood ends.
Have the source service provider block the address
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] A flood harms you by filling your inbound link, so it must be filtered upstream before it reaches your connection. Your own service provider can do this quickly because you have a contract and a support channel with them. The source's provider has no obligation to you, may be hard to identify, and the source addresses are often spoofed or spread across many networks. Blocking at your own firewall happens too late, and blocking all inbound traffic completes the denial of service for the attacker.
optionNotes: Wrong: by the time traffic reaches your firewall, the inbound link is already full.
Correct: your own upstream provider can filter the flood before it consumes your bandwidth, and you can get them to act.
Wrong: blocking all inbound traffic denies service to legitimate users, which is the attacker's goal.
Wrong: you have no relationship with the source's provider, and spoofed or distributed sources make this impractical.

questions.stem: An engineer notices some late collisions on a half-duplex link. The engineer verifies that the devices on both ends of the connection are configured for half duplex. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
options: One of the devices is misconfigured
One of the devices has a hardware issue.
questions.explanation: Late collisions on a link with matched half-duplex settings usually mean the cable is too long, so collisions are detected after the minimum frame time.
optionNotes: Bad termination causes errors rather than late collisions specifically.
Both ends were verified, so misconfiguration is ruled out.
Correct: excessive length causes late collisions.
Hardware faults are less likely than cable length.

questions.stem: A technician wants to install a WAP in the center of a room that provides service in a radius surrounding a radio. Which of the following antenna types should the AP utilize?
questions.explanation: An omnidirectional antenna radiates 360 degrees, covering a radius around a central AP.
optionNotes: Correct: 360-degree coverage from a central point.
Directional antennas focus in one direction.
Yagi is a directional antenna.
Parabolic is highly directional point-to-point.

questions.stem: In an environment where there is not full administrative control over all network connected endpoints, such as a university where non-corporate devices are used, what is the BEST way to restrict access to the network?
options: Use switch port security to limit devices connected to a particular switch port.
Use of virtual local area networks (VLAN) to segregate users.
Use a client-based Network Access Control (NAC) solution.
Use a clientless Network Access Control (NAC) solution
questions.explanation: On unmanaged, non-corporate devices you cannot install agents, so a clientless (agentless) NAC can still assess and restrict them at connection time.
optionNotes: Port security by MAC is easily spoofed and hard to scale.
VLANs segment traffic but do not check devices.
Needs an agent on devices you do not control.
Correct: agentless NAC suits unmanaged endpoints.

questions.stem: An organization is trying to secure instant messaging (IM) communications through its network perimeter. Which of the following is the MOST significant challenge?
options: IM clients can interoperate between multiple vendors.
IM clients can run without administrator privileges.
IM clients can utilize random port numbers.
IM clients can run as executable that do not require installation.
questions.explanation: IM clients hop to random or common open ports, defeating port-based perimeter filtering.
optionNotes: Interoperability is a feature, not a perimeter challenge.
Low privilege matters for endpoints, not perimeter control.
Right: port hopping defeats port-based firewall rules.
Portable executables are an endpoint control issue, less significant at the perimeter.

questions.stem: A Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack was carried out using malware called Mirai to create a large-scale command and control system to launch a botnet. Which of the following devices were the PRIMARY sources used to generate the attack traffic?
options: Web servers running open source operating systems (OS)
questions.explanation: Mirai brute-forced default credentials on IoT devices such as cameras and DVRs to build its botnet.
optionNotes: Right: Mirai infected IoT devices that kept default credentials.
Mirai did not target Windows hosts.
Servers were not the main bot population.
Android was not Mirai's vector.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements BEST distinguishes a stateful packet inspection firewall from a stateless packet filter firewall?
options: The SPI inspects the flags on Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packets.
The SPI inspects the traffic in the context of a session.
The SPI is capable of dropping packets based on a pre-defined rule set.
The SPI inspects traffic on a packet-by-packet basis.
questions.explanation: Stateful inspection tracks connection state and evaluates packets in session context; stateless filters judge each packet alone.
optionNotes: Stateless filters can also inspect flags.
Right: session context is the defining difference.
Both firewall types drop packets by rules.
Packet-by-packet judgment describes stateless filtering.

questions.stem: All hosts on the network are sending logs via syslog-ng to the log collector. The log collector is behind its own firewall, The security professional wants to make sure not to put extra load on the firewall due to the amount of traffic that is passing through it. Which of the following types of filtering would MOST likely be used?
questions.explanation: Static packet filtering checks headers against simple rules with minimal processing, keeping firewall load low.
optionNotes: URL filtering requires heavy application-layer inspection.
Web filtering does not suit syslog traffic and adds load.
Dynamic (stateful) filtering keeps state tables, which adds load.
Right: simple header rules mean the lowest overhead.

questions.stem: When designing a new Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) network, an organization's top concern is preventing unauthorized users accessing the VoIP network. Which of the following will BEST help secure the VoIP network?
questions.explanation: 802.1X port-based NAC authenticates devices before they join the VoIP network.
optionNotes: TLS protects signaling but does not stop network access.
Right: port-based authentication before access.
802.11g is a Wi-Fi speed standard.
A WAF protects web apps, not VoIP access.

questions.stem: Which of the following VPN configurations should be used to separate Internet and corporate traffic?
questions.explanation: A split-tunnel VPN sends only corporate-destined traffic through the tunnel while Internet traffic goes directly out the client's local connection. That is exactly a separation of Internet and corporate traffic.
optionNotes: Correct: routes corporate traffic via tunnel, Internet traffic locally.
An RD gateway brokers remote desktop sessions; it does not split traffic paths.
Site-to-site links two networks; it does not separate a client's Internet traffic.
Out-of-band management is a separate admin channel, not a VPN traffic split.

questions.stem: A corporate security policy specifies that all devices on the network must have updated operating system patches and anti-malware software. Which technology should be used to enforce this policy?
questions.explanation: NAC checks a device's posture (patch level, anti-malware status) before it is admitted to the network and can quarantine non-compliant devices. That directly enforces the stated policy.
optionNotes: NAT translates addresses; it has no view of device health.
Stateful inspection tracks connections, not endpoint patch status.
Packet filtering inspects headers only, not endpoint compliance.
Correct: NAC performs pre-admission posture checks and remediation.

questions.stem: A technician is troubleshooting a client's report about poor wireless performance. Using a client monitor, the technician sees four access points all broadcasting the SSID 'Corporate': RSSI -50 dBm on channel 9, -69 dBm on channel 10, -67 dBm on channel 11, and -63 dBm on channel 6. Which of the following is MOST likely the cause of the issue?
questions.explanation: In the 2.4 GHz band only channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap. Access points on channels 9, 10 and 11 overlap each other, causing co-channel and adjacent-channel interference.
optionNotes: Correct: channels 9, 10 and 11 overlap in 2.4 GHz.
The -50 to -69 dBm readings are usable signal strengths.
Nothing in the readings points to a power misconfiguration.
Antenna type cannot be inferred and the strengths look normal.

questions.stem: A security professional was tasked with rebuilding a company's wireless infrastructure. Which of the following are the MOST important factors to consider while making a decision on which wireless spectrum to deploy?
options: Hybrid frequency band, service set identifier (SSID), and interpolation
Performance, geographic location, and radio signal interference
Facility size, intermodulation, and direct satellite service
Existing client devices, manufacturer reputation, and electrical interference
questions.explanation: The choice of spectrum (2.4, 5 or 6 GHz) depends on the throughput needed, the regulatory rules at the location, and interference in the RF environment.
optionNotes: These are not coherent spectrum selection factors.
Correct: performance, location-based regulation and interference drive the band choice.
Intermodulation and satellite service are marginal here.
Vendor reputation is not a spectrum factor.

questions.stem: What technique used for spoofing the origin of an email can successfully conceal the sender s Internet Protocol (IP) address?
questions.explanation: Onion routing (Tor) passes traffic through several encrypted relays, so the recipient sees only the exit node and not the sender's IP address.
optionNotes: Header fields like In-Reply-To do not hide the IP address.
Crawling is unrelated.
Correct: layered relays conceal the origin IP.
A VPN provider still knows the IP; it is weaker concealment and not the classic answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST secure protocol for remote command access to the firewall?
questions.explanation: SSH provides encrypted, authenticated command-line access to network devices.
optionNotes: Correct: encrypted remote shell
Unauthenticated, cleartext file transfer
Web management, not command access
Cleartext community strings

questions.stem: Which application type is considered high risk and provides a common way for malware and viruses to enter a network?
questions.explanation: P2P file sharing bypasses perimeter controls and distributes unvetted files, a classic malware vector.
optionNotes: Risky but less so
Filtered by mail gateways typically
Correct: high-risk malware vector
Not an application category

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective countermeasure against Man-in-the Middle (MITM) attacks while using online banking?
questions.explanation: Properly implemented TLS with certificate validation authenticates the bank server and protects the session against interception.
optionNotes: Correct: TLS with certificate validation authenticates the bank server
Deprecated and vulnerable
Email protection
Remote shell, not web banking
